summary.intent: Build a full interactive TUI dashboard for the memory-loop feature using Charmbracelet libraries, with tab-based navigation, full memory lifecycle management, injection preview, refresh history, and settings control.
summary.outcome: Completed design phase (spec + implementation plan) and executed Tasks 1-4 via subagent-driven development, scaffolding the full `memorylooptui` package with styles, keys, messages, rendering helpers, root model, placeholder tabs, and the Memories tab with table/filter/detail/lifecycle actions.

repo: Existing CLI uses `termstyle` package with a fixed ANSI 256-color palette (green, red, yellow, cyan, gray, amber) that respects NO_COLOR — TUI should follow this convention rather than introducing custom themes.
Memory lifecycle is managed via `TransitionRecordLifecycle`, `AddManualRecord`, `PruneRecords`, and `SaveState` functions in the `memoryloop` package — these are the mutation surface the TUI wraps.
The project uses a `memoryloop/` package pattern for domain logic separate from `cli/` layer — new TUI follows `memorylooptui/` naming to match existing `insights/`, `settings/` package structure.
`ACCESSIBLE=1` env var triggers simplified output mode in existing huh forms — TUI falls back to plain-text subcommand output in this mode rather than building an accessible TUI variant.
go.mod lint errors on untracked changes are expected during development and not a real lint failure.

code.finding: Entry point for memory-loop subcommands; modified to add the new `tui` subcommand wired to the bubbletea root model.
Defines shared lipgloss styles following termstyle palette conventions for the TUI package.
Defines bubbletea key bindings; mnemonic scheme: a=activate, s=suppress, u=unsuppress, x=archive (avoids conflict with a), P=promote (uppercase avoids conflict).
Shared rendering helpers: tab bar, status bar, strength bar (5-block █ display), time formatting used across all tabs.
Composite bubbletea model holding all four tab sub-models; handles tab switching and delegates Update/View to active tab.

workflow: Subagent-driven development pattern: dispatch one subagent per task group, verify output + run fmt/lint between tasks, then proceed — effective for isolated incremental builds.
Visual companion (local browser server) for TUI design decisions was effective for presenting layout mockups, navigation model comparisons, and keybinding schemes before committing to code.

Brainstorming skill used structured Q&A (5 sequential clarifying questions) to lock down scope, nav model, action depth, tab design, theming, and accessibility before any design work — prevented rework.
Tasks 1-3 dispatched as a single implementer agent since they were tightly coupled foundational scaffolding with no benefit to splitting.
Spec self-review step caught a missing `prune` keybinding before the spec was finalized.

friction: go.mod lint error flagged during verification was a false alarm (untracked go.mod changes not yet committed) — required manual diagnosis to confirm it was benign.
Tab key naming conflict: both 'activate' and 'archive' start with 'a', requiring 'x' as an unintuitive workaround for archive.
open_items: Tasks 5-9 not yet implemented: Injection tab (log + prompt tester), History tab (refresh history + trigger), Settings tab (mode/policy/max cycling), Add Memory form (inline text inputs), and final polish/verification.
Accessible TUI mode deferred — current plan falls back to plain-text subcommands when ACCESSIBLE=1; a proper screen-reader-friendly TUI variant is noted as future work.
prune action was added to spec but keybinding scheme needs to be confirmed in implementation — ensure it doesn't conflict with existing keys.
Manual verification checklist (Task 9) not yet run — full end-to-end testing of the TUI against a real memory-loop state file still pending.
